doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: What playing free means, and trad and bebop purists
summary: Free means playing like yourself; he describes trad sessions and bebop factories in New York and why a wide palette prevents purism.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: Right. That little bit of information is a lot of comfort.
I was — when you talk about playing free, that means you have so many choices that sometimes you’re stymied. There’s too many choices.

Yeah. Free to me means play like yourself. You know. I’m kind of like a music — a lot of us musicians, as I’m sure you’re the same, we love lots of music. We have a wide palette. We’ve listened to things. I get a big kick out of music, just all different kinds of music in the world, but you know, when you’re doing something, when they say “free” that means you have license to do whatever you want. So I think your real tendencies come out when you’re in the mindset of playing free you know, as opposed to being with, maybe you’ll find yourself in a group of musicians that are very specific in their tastes. Okay? So they have what they call “trad” bands in New York City and New Orleans. And I’ve been to trad sessions in New York City and you go in and everybody’s, it’s almost like a, like a, it’s like you walk into a roomful of anachronisms you know and there’s everybody with their old hairstyle with the — the whole thing, the whole ball of wax.

It really is. It really is. I’m saying wow, they’re committed. And then all the musicians are playing, sounding beautiful, no bebop in the language, no R&B into the language. And I really admired that and realized — and it’s the same thing if you go to Small’s in New York at times, depending on who’s there, but some of these places are known as
bebop factories. And there are people that are very specific in their approach. So for me and for a lot of musicians I think that, the wide range of influences, prevents us from being purists.
